what: Valero is one of the largest independent oil refiners in the world. It buys crude oil, turns it into petrol, diesel and jet fuel at refineries on the US Gulf Coast and elsewhere, and is also a large producer of renewable diesel and ethanol.
customers: Fuel wholesalers, retailers, airlines and industrial buyers across North America and in export markets.
money: 15 refineries producing petrol, diesel and jet fuel
the Diamond Green Diesel joint venture
corn ethanol plants in the Midwest
moat: Gulf Coast refineries with deepwater access that can process cheap heavy crude and export finished fuel, an advantage few refiners have.
risks: Profit depends on the refining margin between crude and fuel, which swings violently
Revenue has fallen about 11% a year over three years as fuel prices came down
Renewable diesel economics depend on government credits
Refineries need periodic expensive maintenance shutdowns
opportunities: Little new refining capacity is being built in the West, supporting margins
Low debt relative to peers at about $11 billion against $10 billion of cash
Large buybacks return most free cash flow to shareholders
watch: Refining margin per barrel and throughput volumes.
